extracted.intended_audience: energy regulators, energy lawyers, NERC/FERC stakeholders, and industry compliance personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory/regulatory criteria for how the Electric Reliability Organization (NERC) should develop reliability standards and how FERC will review, approve, direct modification of, or remand those standards under FPA §215. Includes registration thresholds for inverter-based resources and procedural expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of inverter-based resources by aggregated impact
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC found that inverter-based resources connected to the Bulk-Power System, regardless of size, that in the aggregate have a material impact on Bulk-Power System performance should be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC supported the aggregated approach with NERC event reports and evidence of rapid growth of inverter-based resources; it adopted an aggregation rationale (aggregate response to a single normally cleared fault can result in tripping/momentary cessation). Commenters could challenge factual support; FERC relied on NERC to develop thresholds subject to FERC approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for registration (60 kV) to distinguish bulk vs distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: NERC proposed, and FERC accepted, a 60 kV connection threshold as appropriate to ensure non-Bulk Electric System inverter-based resources material to BPS reliability are subject to registration while excluding distribution-system resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC provided detailed analysis supporting the 60 kV threshold; commenters argued 60 kV could capture distribution-level facilities, but FERC concluded NERC's explanation was adequate. Entities may challenge registrations if they believe they should be excluded as local distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration scope — exclusion (but not prohibition) of distribution-connected resources
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC articulated that its registration plan pertained only to inverter-based resources connected to the bulk-power system and not those connected to the distribution system, though it did not definitively rule out future registration of distribution-connected resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC took distribution-level registration 'off the table' in that instance but left open the possibility depending on future factual record and reliability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulk-Power System jurisdiction test — 'needed to maintain transmission system reliability'
rubrics_metrics.description: To assert FPA §215 jurisdiction, FERC must demonstrate that electric energy from a source is injected into the interconnected transmission system and is in sufficient quantity that it is 'needed to maintain transmission system reliability.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rationale could extend to distributed generation, aggregators, offshore wind, or large loads if the record shows the energy is needed for reliability. FERC needs a supportive record demonstrating specific reliability challenges to assert authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERO procedural requirements for standards development
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERO must have a standards development process that 'provide[s] for reasonable notice and opportunity for public comment, due process, openness, and balance of interests.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirement under FPA §215(d)(1). FERC has indicated an ANSI-accredited process 'is one reasonable means' to satisfy this but cautioned about timeliness concerns with ANSI processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC statutory approval standard for reliability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC may approve a proposed reliability standard if it determines the standard is 'just, reasonable, not unduly discriminatory or preferential, and in the public interest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This legal standard (FPA §215(d)(2)) governs FERC review. FERC also must give 'due weight' to ERO technical expertise but will not defer with respect to the effect of a standard on competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must be designed to achieve a specified reliability goal
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed reliability standard 'must be designed to achieve a specified reliability goal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC guidance (Order No. 672) emphasizes that standards should have a concrete reliability objective; the petition should explain how the standard achieves that goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must contain a technically sound means to achieve the goal
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed standard 'must contain a technically sound means to achieve this goal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC expects technical justification and evidence that the requirements will accomplish the stated reliability objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and unambiguity regarding requirements and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed standard 'should be clear and unambiguous regarding what is required and who is required to comply.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC looks for unambiguous obligations and clearly identified responsible entities to ensure enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must provide a clear criterion or measure of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed standard should provide 'a clear criterion or measure of whether an entity is in compliance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC expects measurable, enforceable compliance metrics and not vague or unenforceable requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and efficiency over 'best practice' optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed standard 'need not necessarily reflect the optimal method, or ‘best practice,’ for achieving its reliability goal' but 'should achieve its reliability goal effectively and efficiently.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC accepts multiple methods so long as they achieve the reliability objective; the standard need not be the theoretically optimal approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the 'lowest common denominator' compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed standard must 'not simply reflect a compromise . . . based on the least effective North American practice — the so-called 'lowest common denominator' — if such practice does not adequately protect Bulk-Power System reliability.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC warned against watering down standards for consensus if that results in inadequate protection of reliability; cost cannot justify reducing reliability below what is adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of compliance costs (legitimate but not dispositive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of compliance is a legitimate consideration when developing standards, but it 'should not drive down the quality of standards to the lowest common denominator.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC permits cost considerations but expects reliability protection to remain primary; the petition should explain cost impacts without undermining reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due weight to ERO technical expertise — ERO must justify standards
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC will give 'due weight to the technical expertise of the [ERO] with respect to the content of a proposed standard,' but this does not create a rebuttable presumption of acceptance; the ERO 'must justify to the Commission' that a proposed standard meets statutory criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC expects NERC to include rationale and supporting evidence in petitions; disputes have arisen over whether FERC sufficiently respects 'due weight.'

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC's four review options for proposed standards
rubrics_metrics.description: When presented with a petition, FERC identified four options: (1) approve; (2) approve as mandatory and enforceable and direct modification pursuant to §215(d)(5); (3) request additional information; or (4) remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC has often used option (2) — approve plus direct modifications — allowing the standard to take effect while NERC develops directed changes. FERC has rarely remanded standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC authority to direct ERO to submit a new/modified standard under §215(d)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under FPA §215(d)(5), 'The Commission... may order the [ERO] to submit to the Commission a proposed reliability standard or a modification... that addresses a specific matter' if FERC considers it appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC does not dictate the specific text but tasks the ERO to address the concern. In practice, FERC often issues detailed directives and may set deadlines for NERC to submit modifications, subject to reasonableness and preserving stakeholder processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for ERO submission of standards must be reasonable and preserve stakeholder process
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC regulations allow the Commission to set deadlines for the ERO to submit new or modified standards (e.g., when remanding or directing under §215(d)(5)), but such deadlines 'must be reasonable and cannot preclude a stakeholder process required by FPA §215(c)(2).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC has set deadlines when concerned about timeliness; on rehearing it explained deadlines are consistent with statutory authority but must allow required stakeholder deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANSI-accredited process as a reasonable means (but not dispositive) to satisfy procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC in Order No. 672 explained that an ANSI-accredited process 'is one reasonable means' of satisfying the statutory provision requiring notice, comment, due process, openness, and balance of interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC expressed apprehension about ANSI process timeliness and explicitly rejected creating a rebuttable presumption that ANSI-developed standards automatically satisfy FERC review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence/support requirement for alternative proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ERO proposes an 'equivalent alternative' to a Commission example or directive, NERC must provide 'adequate support that fully explains how the alternative produces a result that is as effective as or more effective than the Commission’s example or directive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC seeks sufficient explanation and technical support to accept alternatives rather than prescriptive language; this underlies NERC's responsibility to justify its approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERO statutory capability to develop and enforce standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The certified ERO must have the ability to 'develop and enforce . . . reliability standards that provide for an adequate level of reliability of the bulk-power system.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This foundational statutory mandate under §215(c)(1) and (c)(2)(D) requires both standards-writing capacity and enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved standards take effect only after FERC approval; disapproval triggers remand
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability standards proposed by the ERO take effect only after FERC approval; if FERC disapproves a proposed standard 'in whole or in part,' it must remand the standard to the ERO 'for further consideration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural rule establishes FERC's final say on taking effect; remand requires NERC to revise and resubmit the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness expectation for NERC response to FERC directives
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC has expressed concern about NERC's pace in responding to directives and has expected NERC to respond within reasonable timelines (NERC had estimated 12-15 months for many standards but actual averages were longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC criticized that after three years NERC had responded to only ~15% of directives and has used orders and deadlines to improve timeliness; industry has raised resource/balloting concerns about speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vegetation management standard principle — defense-in-depth
rubrics_metrics.description: FAC-003-5 (Transmission Vegetation Management) requires transmission owners to apply a 'defense‐in‐depth strategy to manage vegetation' located on and adjacent to transmission rights-of-way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an example of how standards translate causal findings (trees, tools, training) into a mandatory approach to reduce risk; NERC maintains statistics and reports on vegetation-related incidents.
